meta.description: Illustrative model evaluation for software engineering on an NVIDIA RTX 3060 12GB desktop
meta.data_nature: All benchmark ratings and token generation figures are illustrative engineering estimates based on hardware specifications and theoretical bandwidth calculations.

user_input.task: Interactive code assistant for full-stack TypeScript and Python, integration tests, and repository refactoring in VS Code
user_input.target_runtime: Ollama with Continue.dev VS Code extension

hardware_budget_analysis.feasibility_assessment: 12GB VRAM is sufficient to host a 7B-14B parameter model quantized to 4-bit or 5-bit precision with an 8k-16k token context window entirely within VRAM, delivering high interactive token generation speeds (30-60 tok/s).

strengths: State-of-the-art coding benchmark performance in 14B class
Strong TypeScript/Python syntax and test generation
limitations: At 8k context (FP16) or 16k context (Q8_0 KV cache), model and cache take ~10.5GB VRAM, filling available VRAM on a 12GB card. If unquantized FP16 KV cache is run at 16k context (3.2GB cache), total memory reaches 12.1GB, exceeding VRAM.

strengths: Accommodates 16k context in FP16 with 3.3GB VRAM headroom to spare
Low VRAM pressure allows running a simultaneous embedding model
limitations: Lower reasoning depth on complex multi-file architectural refactoring compared to the 14B variant

candidate_comparison.estimated_speed_range_tok_per_sec: 4 - 8 (with partial layer offloading across PCIe 4.0 and DDR4 RAM)
strengths: Frontier-grade open coding model quality competing with proprietary models
limitations: Requires offloading ~12GB of weights to system DDR4 RAM, collapsing generation speed below comfortable interactive typing rates

best_fit.rationale: Represents the maximum coding intelligence achievable entirely inside 12GB VRAM without CPU-RAM offloading penalties. When deployed with an 8k context window (or 16k with Q8_0 KV cache enabled), it safely stays within the 10.4GB usable VRAM ceiling.
best_fit.trade_offs: To avoid Windows Sysmem Fallback thrashing, restrict context to 8,192 tokens under default FP16 KV cache in Ollama, or enable quantized KV caching for 16k tokens.

alternative_speed.rationale: Recommended if ultra-low latency autocomplete or concurrent browser/editor GPU load is prioritized. Consumes only ~6.8GB VRAM at 32k context, leaving generous headroom.

alternative_quality.rationale: Viable for deep offline batch refactoring or complex code audits where generation speeds of 4-6 tok/s are acceptable in exchange for frontier reasoning.

installation_commands: # Ensure Ollama is installed on Windows, then pull the primary recommendation
# Set context window to 16k in Continue.dev config or Ollama Modelfile

validation_test_procedure.diagnostic_prompt: Write an asynchronous TypeScript function that fetches paginated data from an API endpoint with exponential backoff retry logic. Include typing for errors.
validation_test_procedure.expected_verification: Verify that VRAM usage in Task Manager / nvidia-smi stabilizes under 10.5GB, generation starts immediately without disk paging thrash, and code compiles without syntax errors.

deployment_and_validation.cloud_fallback_criteria: If full-repository analysis exceeding 64,000 tokens is required with multi-step debugging across hundreds of files, fall back to Claude 3.5 Sonnet / Claude 3.7 Sonnet via API, as local 12GB VRAM cannot support 100k+ context without severe memory exhaustion.
